issues.title: Rekrut AI - Product Vision and Master Roadmap
issues.body:
## What we are building

Rekrut AI is an **all-in-one, end-to-end hiring platform** with a transparent credit-score-style rating for **both sides** of the market:

- **OmniScore** rates candidates across 8 factors, and the candidate can see it, understand it, and improve it.
- **TrustScore** rates companies on how they actually behave when hiring, so candidates know who to trust before they apply.

Everything is built in-house. No Checkr, no DocuSign, no HackerRank, no HireVue. One platform, one data model, no per-transaction fees.

## Why this matters

The hiring market is broken and AI made it worse:

| Finding | Source |
|---|---|
| Only 11% of candidates rate their experience as very positive, down from 18% in 2023 | PeopleScout 2026 |
| 42% of ghosted candidates were ghosted 3+ times | Lever 2026 |
| 60% do not know whether a human ever read their resume | Monster 2026 |
| 70% were never told AI would evaluate them | Greenhouse 2026 |
| 26% of Black applicants applied to roles where the AI adversely impacted their group | Stanford HAI 2026 |

Stanford found that a single vendor's score follows a candidate across 156+ employers for up to 330 days. One low score means rejection everywhere, and the candidate can neither see it nor dispute it.

That is a credit score with none of the consumer protections. Rekrut AI makes the score visible, explainable, improvable, and owned by the candidate.

## The full pipeline

**Candidate:** create profile -> match jobs -> apply -> screening -> aptitude test -> technical test -> interview scheduling -> manager interview -> offer letter -> accept -> document verification (BGC) -> onboarding -> payroll

**Recruiter:** create company profile (company email only) -> get approved by the company account owner -> post jobs -> review candidates -> run screening -> assign assessments -> schedule interviews -> send offers -> verify documents -> manage onboarding -> run payroll

## Roadmap

| Phase | Name | Effort | Milestone |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Critical Bug Fixes | 40h | Stabilise |
| 1 | MVP Launch | 80h | First real users |
| 2 | Structured Screening | 230h | Screening + OmniScore v2 |
| 3 | Technical Assessment | 280h | Code sandbox (the moat) |
| 4 | Interview Excellence | 240h | Panel video + analytics |
| 5 | Secure Hiring | 200h | BGC + e-signature |
| 6 | Enterprise Complete | 265h | Permissions + API |

Total: ~1335 hours, ~33 weeks.

## Architecture decisions (locked)

| Area | Choice |
|---|---|
| Code sandbox | Docker + Judge0, full language support |
| Video | LiveKit, self-hosted |
| E-signature | In-house PKCS#7 + timestamp authority |
| Analytics store | PostgreSQL for operations, ClickHouse for analytics |
| Monitoring | Prometheus + Grafana + Loki, self-hosted |
| Test coverage target | 95% E2E |

## Explicitly out of scope

White-label, regional languages, native mobile apps, and every third-party integration (ATS, job boards, payroll partners, BGC vendors, e-signature vendors).

## Reference documents

- `docs/reports/STRATEGIC_MARKET_ANALYSIS.md`
- `docs/reports/CEO_REVIEW_SUMMARY.md`
- `docs/qa/live-qa-2026-08-08/REPORT.md`

issues.title: Fix infinite render loops firing up to 1,255 API calls per page view
issues.body:
## Problem

14 pages re-render without bound and hammer the API for as long as the tab stays open. Measured on a fresh account with no data over a single ~32 second visit.

**Recruiter**

| Page | API calls | Worst endpoint |
|---|---|---|
| `/recruiter/candidates` | 1,255 | `saved-searches` x483 |
| `/recruiter/jobs/new` | 653 | `GET /api/countries` x644 |
| `/recruiter/job-create` | 648 | `GET /api/countries` x640 |
| `/recruiter/offers` | 548 | `candidates` x180 |
| `/recruiter/assessments` | 447 | `recruiter/catalog` x108 |
| `/recruiter/applications` | 366 | `recruiter/jobs` x178 |
| `/recruiter/company` | 366 | `company/team/members` x179 |
| `/recruiter/onboarding-docs` | 343 | `onboarding/recruiter/summary` x335 |
| `/recruiter/jobs` | 177 | `recruiter/jobs` x169 |
| `/recruiter/omniscore` | 71 | `omniscore/company-dashboard` x63 |

**Candidate**

| Page | API calls | Worst endpoint |
|---|---|---|
| `/candidate/omniscore` | 286 | `POST omniscore/checkin` x70 |
| `/candidate/onboarding` | 188 | `onboarding/wizard/progress` x180 |
| `/candidate/offers` | 185 | `onboarding/offers/me` x177 |
| `/candidate/profile` | 81 | `candidate/profile` x73 |

`/recruiter/candidates` sustains roughly 39 requests per second per open tab. `/candidate/omniscore` issues 70 POST writes per visit to a non-idempotent endpoint.

## Root cause

The loader is declared as a plain `async function` in the component body, so it gets a new reference on every render, and it is listed as a `useEffect` dependency. The effect re-runs after every render, sets state, triggers another render, recreates the function, re-runs the effect.

Confirmed instances:

| File | Effect dependency |
|---|---|
| `client/src/pages/candidate/omniscore.tsx:266` | `loadMyScore` |
| `client/src/pages/candidate/profile.tsx:224` | `loadProfile` |
| `client/src/pages/candidate/offers.tsx:81` | `loadOffers` |
| `client/src/pages/candidate/onboarding.tsx:1368` | `loadProgress` |
| `client/src/pages/candidate/screening.tsx:70` | `loadScreening` |

The recruiter pages show identical behaviour and need the same audit.

## Fix

Wrap each loader in `useCallback` with a stable dependency array, matching what `jobs.tsx`, `applications.tsx` and `ai-coaching.tsx` already do correctly. Alternatively drop the function from the dependency array and run on mount only.

## Prevention

- Enable the `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` lint rule
- Add a CI test asserting a bounded request count per page, using the counter in `docs/qa/live-qa-2026-08-08/qa_lib.py`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every page in both tables above fires fewer than 20 requests on load
- [ ] Zero repeated POST writes on `/candidate/omniscore`
- [ ] `/api/countries` fetched at most once per page
- [ ] Lint rule enabled and CI regression test added

Effort: ~4h

issues.title: Candidates cannot apply from the job board drawer - the default path is a dead end
issues.body:
## Reproduction

1. Sign in as a candidate, open `/candidate/jobs`
2. Click any job card, the slide-out drawer opens
3. Click **Apply Now** in the drawer

**Expected:** the application form opens.

**Actual:** the browser navigates to `/candidate/jobs/174?apply=true` and the form stays closed. No error, no form, no network request. The candidate gets no indication anything failed.

Applying from the standalone page does work, so the feature is functional but the entry point users actually take is broken. This is the default interaction path.

## Root cause

The drawer navigates with a query parameter:

```
client/src/pages/candidate/jobs.tsx:1091
onApply={() => {
  if (selectedJob) navigate(`/candidate/jobs/${selectedJob.id}?apply=true`)
}}
```

`client/src/pages/candidate/job-detail.tsx` never reads it. The file contains no `useSearchParams`, no `location.search`, no `URLSearchParams`. The form is gated purely on local state at line 984.

Regression introduced with the job detail drawer, commit `c33bbb9`, issue #31 / PR #73.

## Fix

In `job-detail.tsx`, read the query parameter on mount and call `setShowApplyForm(true)` when `apply=true` is present.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Clicking Apply Now in the drawer opens the application form
- [ ] Submitting produces `POST /api/candidate/jobs/:id/apply -> 200`
- [ ] The application appears in the candidate's Applications list and the recruiter's view
- [ ] E2E test covers the drawer path, not just the standalone page

Effort: ~1h

issues.title: Staging is wired to LIVE Stripe keys - real charges are possible
issues.body:
## Problem

Clicking **Start checkout** on `/pricing` while signed in on staging produced a live-mode Stripe session:

```
POST https://rekrutai-staging.onrender.com/api/billing/checkout-session -> 200
-> https://checkout.stripe.com/c/pay/cs_live_b1ikxByCEsCMPaq4NyZKoElmJ6pXJwjDrhRGvh8G5qG0IPfijTUM9xqxwz...
```

The `cs_live_` prefix confirms live mode. The hosted page read "Subscribe to Starter - Rekrut AI, $29.00 per month".

## Impact

- Anyone testing billing on staging with a real card is charged real money
- Stripe test cards are rejected, so the billing path cannot be QA'd at all

## Fix

Point the staging Render service at `sk_test_` / `pk_test_` keys and a test-mode price ID. Add a startup assertion that refuses to boot a non-production environment holding a live key.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Staging checkout produces a `cs_test_` session
- [ ] Stripe test cards complete checkout end to end on staging
- [ ] Server refuses to start if `NODE_ENV != production` and the Stripe key starts with `sk_live_`
- [ ] Production separately confirmed to hold live keys

Relates to #6.

Effort: ~30m

issues.title: No email provider on staging - password reset links only reach the server console
issues.body:
## Problem

`POST /api/auth/forgot-password` returns 200 but the confirmation screen reads:

> **Check your console** - For testing purposes (no email API key configured), the password reset link has been logged to the server console.

No transactional email can leave staging, so reset, invites, offer letters and notifications cannot be verified before release.

## Scope

- Configure a transactional provider (Postmark or Resend) on staging and production
- Verify the 6 existing templates render and deliver
- Add delivery logging so failures are visible rather than silent
- Confirm production delivery separately, it was not exercised in the read-only pass

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Password reset email is delivered to a real inbox from staging
- [ ] Application received, interview scheduled, offer sent, and status change emails deliver
- [ ] Send failures are logged and surfaced, never swallowed
- [ ] Email delivery covered by an E2E test using a catch-all inbox

issues.title: Analytics events fail sitewide with 403 CSRF_INVALID
issues.body:
## Problem

`POST /api/analytics/events` returns `403 CSRF_INVALID` on every page across the whole site. No product analytics are being recorded, so we are flying blind on funnel, activation and retention.

Confirmed still reproducible in the 2026-08-08 sweep. Previously filed as #49.

## Fix

Ensure the analytics client attaches the CSRF token the same way the rest of the authenticated API client does, or exempt the analytics endpoint if it carries no state-changing risk and is otherwise authenticated.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `POST /api/analytics/events` returns 200 for authenticated and anonymous visitors
- [ ] Signup, login, job apply, checkout and assessment start events are recorded
- [ ] A dashboard query confirms events land in the database

Effort: ~3h

issues.title: Remove fabricated recruiter data - fake saved searches and invented trend percentages
issues.body:
## Problem

On a brand-new recruiter account with exactly one applicant, `/recruiter/candidates` renders data that does not exist:

- **Fabricated saved searches.** Chips labelled "Senior Engineers - Remote" and "High Match - Frontend" are hardcoded, despite the account never creating a search and `GET /api/recruiter/saved-searches` returning 404.
- **Fabricated trend deltas.** "+12%", "+8%", "-0%", "+15%", "+5%" on an account with no history.
- **List never renders.** Summary cards correctly read "Total Candidates 1", but the list below stays as skeleton loaders forever, a direct consequence of the render loop.

The applicant who applied to this recruiter's own job never appears, even though the same application shows on `/recruiter/applications`.

This is a trust problem. A platform whose entire pitch is transparent scoring cannot ship invented numbers.

Confirms #15 and #69 are still open, and extends them with the saved-searches fabrication.

## Scope

Audit Dashboard, Candidates and Analytics on the recruiter side. Replace every hardcoded value with either real data or a proper empty state.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No hardcoded saved searches, trends, or counts anywhere in the recruiter UI
- [ ] Empty states shown when there is genuinely no data
- [ ] The candidate list renders real applicants
- [ ] A grep for placeholder percentage strings returns nothing in `client/src/pages/recruiter/`

Effort: ~3h

issues.title: Enforce company email domain on recruiter registration
issues.body:
## Problem

Anyone can register as a recruiter with any email address and claim to represent any company. There is nothing stopping someone signing up as `recruiter@google.com` with a Gmail account, or creating a duplicate "Acme Inc" that competes with the real one.

## Requirement

A recruiter may only create or join a company profile using an email address on that company's verified domain.

## Scope

- Block free/disposable email providers (gmail, yahoo, outlook, mailinator, and similar) on recruiter registration
- Derive the company domain from the recruiter's email address
- Verify domain ownership for the first recruiter of a company, via a DNS TXT record or an email challenge to a role address
- If the domain already maps to an existing company, route the new recruiter into the approval workflow rather than creating a duplicate company
- Store the verified domain on the company record and enforce it on every subsequent join

## Edge cases to handle

- Company uses multiple domains (allow the owner to add verified aliases)
- Recruitment agencies hiring on behalf of others (flag for manual review, do not silently allow)
- Subdomain addresses such as `@careers.acme.com`
- Email address changes after verification

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Registration with a free email provider is rejected with a clear message
- [ ] First recruiter on a domain must complete domain verification before posting a job
- [ ] Second recruiter on the same domain is routed to approval, not to a new company
- [ ] Verified domain is stored and enforced
- [ ] Tests cover each edge case above

Depends on nothing. Blocks recruiter approval workflow.

Effort: ~8h

issues.title: Recruiter approval workflow - company owner approves new team members
issues.body:
## Requirement

When a new recruiter registers on a domain that already has a company account, they land in a pending state. The company account owner approves or rejects them. Only approved recruiters can post jobs, view candidates, or act on applications.

## Scope

**States:** `pending` -> `approved` | `rejected` | `suspended`

- Pending recruiters see a holding screen explaining they are awaiting approval
- Owner receives an email and an in-app notification for each pending request
- Owner sees a pending-requests queue with the requester's name, email, and signup time
- Owner can approve, reject with a reason, or suspend an existing member
- Every pending recruiter is blocked from all write operations and all candidate data
- Audit log records who approved or rejected whom and when
- The first recruiter on a verified domain automatically becomes the owner

## Authorization

This is a security boundary, not a UX nicety. Enforcement must live in middleware on the server, not in the client. Every recruiter route must check approval state.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Pending recruiter cannot reach any recruiter API endpoint, verified by test
- [ ] Owner receives email and in-app notification on new request
- [ ] Approve, reject and suspend all work and are audit logged
- [ ] Rejected recruiter sees the reason
- [ ] Ownership transfer is possible so a company is never orphaned
- [ ] Tests cover privilege escalation attempts from a pending account

Depends on company email domain enforcement.

Effort: ~16h

issues.title: Post-auth redirect takes 6.1 seconds on every login and signup
issues.body:
## Problem

After a successful login or signup the redirect to the dashboard consistently takes 6.1 seconds. Measured repeatedly in the 2026-08-08 sweep, it is not variance.

Six seconds of dead time on the very first interaction is the worst possible place to be slow. Previously filed as #70.

## Investigation needed

- Is the delay server-side (token issue, session write, migration check) or client-side (bundle parse, blocking fetch waterfall)?
- The main bundle is 1.55MB, which is a likely contributor on first load
- Check whether the dashboard blocks on several sequential API calls before painting

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Post-auth redirect completes in under 2 seconds at p95
- [ ] Root cause documented in the issue before the fix lands
- [ ] A performance regression test asserts the budget

Effort: ~4h

issues.title: Unknown routes return HTTP 200 instead of 404
issues.body:
## Problem

`https://rekrutai.co/this-route-does-not-exist` returns HTTP 200 with the SPA shell. Confirmed on production.

## Impact

- Search engines index nonexistent pages
- Monitoring cannot distinguish a broken link from a working page
- Job posting structured data will be polluted with dead URLs

## Fix

The SPA fallback should return 404 for paths the client router does not recognise. Maintain a known-route list on the server, or have the client signal not-found and set the status via a prerender layer.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Unknown paths return HTTP 404 with the branded not-found page
- [ ] Known SPA routes still return 200
- [ ] Test covers both cases

Previously filed as #48.

Effort: ~2h

issues.title: Video interview page shows a raw error card when opened directly
issues.body:
## Problem

Navigating directly to `/candidate/video-interview` renders a bare **"Error - No interview ID provided"** card. The route is registered in `App.tsx` and therefore reachable, but has no graceful empty state.

## Fix

Show an empty state that explains there is no interview selected and links to the candidate's scheduled interviews.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Direct visit shows a helpful empty state, not an error card
- [ ] The empty state links to `/candidate/interviews`

issues.title: EPIC Phase 2 - Structured Screening
issues.body:
Turn Rekrut AI from a job board into a structured hiring pipeline. This is the first phase that delivers real differentiation.

**Delivers**
- Screening questions per job
- Timed aptitude tests
- AI Recruiter Screener
- OmniScore v2 deep scoring
- Working chat on both sides

**Announcement:** "Now with AI-powered screening"

Effort: ~230h

issues.title: Implement 10 API endpoints the frontend calls but which do not exist
issues.body:
## Problem

Ten endpoints referenced by the client return `404 {"error":"API endpoint not found"}` and have no handler anywhere in `routes/`. Every call site swallows the error in an empty `catch {}`, so each one silently disables a feature with no visible failure.

| Endpoint | Called from | Feature disabled |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/recruiter/saved-searches` | `/recruiter/candidates` | Saved searches, called 483x per visit |
| `GET /api/recruiter/screenings` | `/recruiter/screening` | Recruiter screening |
| `GET /api/recruiter/conversations` | `/recruiter/chat` | Recruiter messaging |
| `GET /api/candidate/conversations` | `/candidate/chat` | Candidate messaging |
| `GET /api/conversations/:id/messages` | both chat pages | Message threads |
| `GET /api/careers/default` | `/recruiter/career-page` | Public careers page |
| `GET /api/candidate/list` | `/recruiter/onboarding-ai` | AI onboarding |
| `GET /api/candidate/documents` | `/candidate/documents` | Document management |
| `GET /api/onboarding/feedback/completed` | `/candidate/feedback` | Post-hire feedback |
| `GET /api/omniscore/explainer` | `/candidate/omniscore` | "Why this score?" |

Both sides of chat are entirely non-functional, and the explainability endpoint is missing on the feature that is supposed to be our core differentiator.

## Scope

For each endpoint, either implement it or remove the UI that depends on it. Do not leave dead call sites.

Separately, replace the empty `catch {}` blocks with real error surfacing so the next missing endpoint is visible immediately.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All ten endpoints return 200 with correct data, or their UI is removed
- [ ] No empty `catch {}` around API calls in the client
- [ ] Failed API calls surface a toast or inline error
- [ ] A CI check fails the build if the client references an unrouted API path

Effort: ~40h

issues.title: Screening questions - custom per-job questionnaire with AI evaluation
issues.body:
## Requirement

Step 4 of the candidate pipeline. After applying, a candidate answers a short set of screening questions defined by the recruiter for that job. This is the Crossover "Basic Fit Check" equivalent.

## Recruiter side

- Define screening questions when creating or editing a job
- Question types: single choice, multiple choice, short text, yes/no, numeric
- Mark questions as knockout (a wrong answer auto-rejects with a clear reason)
- AI suggests questions based on the job description
- Set a pass threshold

## Candidate side

- Screening opens immediately after applying
- Progress is saved, the candidate can pause and resume
- Clear disclosure that AI evaluates the answers, per our transparency principle
- Result and reason are shown to the candidate, whether pass or fail

## AI evaluation

- Free-text answers scored against the job requirements
- Every score carries a written explanation
- Recruiter can override any AI decision, and the override is audit logged

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Recruiter can attach questions to a job and set knockouts
- [ ] Candidate completes screening, can pause and resume
- [ ] AI scores free text and explains each score
- [ ] Knockout answers auto-reject with a reason shown to the candidate
- [ ] Recruiter override is possible and audit logged
- [ ] Candidate is told AI is evaluating before they start

Builds on `routes/screening.js` and migration 022/051. Depends on the missing endpoints issue.

Effort: ~24h

issues.title: Aptitude test engine - timed cognitive assessment
issues.body:
## Requirement

Step 5 of the pipeline. A timed, standardised cognitive aptitude test, equivalent to Crossover's CCAT. Fifteen minutes, randomised questions, covering logic, verbal reasoning and numerical problem solving.

Crossover uses this because cognitive aptitude predicts real-world performance better than a resume does, and it lets a global pool be shortlisted fairly.

## Scope

- Question bank across logic, verbal and numerical categories, with difficulty ratings
- Randomised selection so no two candidates get an identical paper
- Hard countdown timer with auto-submit, resilient to refresh and disconnect
- Per-role target score ranges set by the recruiter
- Retake policy, configurable, defaulting to six months
- Immediate scoring and percentile against the candidate pool
- Result feeds the OmniScore "verified skills" factor

## Anti-cheat, basic tier

Full proctoring is a separate Phase 3 issue. Here we need only tab-switch detection, copy-paste tracking, and timing anomaly flags.

## Fairness

This is a high-risk AI use under the EU AI Act. Score distributions must be monitored per demographic group and reported in the compliance dashboard.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Timer cannot be defeated by refresh, disconnect, or clock manipulation
- [ ] Auto-submit on expiry preserves answers already given
- [ ] Randomised papers, no duplicate question sets
- [ ] Percentile calculated against the real pool
- [ ] Retake lockout enforced server-side
- [ ] Score distribution by group visible in the compliance dashboard

Builds on `routes/assessments.js` and migration 031 question bank.

Effort: ~24h

issues.title: AI Recruiter Screener - evaluate candidates against the job with full explanation
issues.body:
## Requirement

The recruiter-side counterpart to the candidate AI coach, and one of the two headline features of Phase 2. Approved in the CEO review as a scope expansion.

## What it does

- Analyses the candidate profile against the job requirements
- Produces a fit score with a written explanation of every component
- Breaks the score into skills, experience and culture fit
- Generates screening and interview questions tailored to that specific candidate's background
- Flags red flags: employment gaps, timeline inconsistencies, claims unsupported by evidence
- Recommends **Interview**, **Reject**, or **More Info**, always with reasons
- Supplies talking points for the hiring manager

## Non-negotiable constraints

This is exactly the kind of tool that Stanford found producing systemic rejection at other vendors. Ours must not repeat that:

- The recommendation is advisory. A human makes the decision, and the UI must make that obvious.
- Every score component carries an explanation the recruiter can read.
- The candidate can see that AI screening occurred and can request human review.
- Recommendations are logged with inputs and outputs for audit.
- Adverse impact is measured per job posting, not aggregated across the platform. Aggregated audits are precisely how bias gets hidden.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Fit score with per-component explanation
- [ ] Generated questions are specific to the candidate, not generic
- [ ] Red flags cite the evidence that triggered them
- [ ] Recommendation is clearly advisory, human decision required
- [ ] Every recommendation logged with inputs and outputs
- [ ] Per-posting adverse impact reporting available
- [ ] Candidate can request human review

Builds on `lib/recruiter-screener.js`.

Effort: ~50h

issues.title: OmniScore v2 - deep multi-factor scoring with explainability
issues.body:
## Why this is the most important issue in the roadmap

OmniScore is the product. Everything else is a hiring platform that many companies already sell. The transparent, portable, explainable score is the thing no competitor offers.

Stanford's 2026 study of 4 million applications found that a hidden vendor score follows a candidate across 156+ employers for up to 330 days, and that 10% of candidates applying to four or more roles were rejected from every single one. Candidates cannot see those scores or dispute them. That is a credit score with none of the consumer protections that credit scores gained through regulation.

OmniScore v2 is our answer. v1 is 160 lines of basic calculation and is not defensible.

## The 8 factors

| Factor | Weight | Sources |
|---|---|---|
| Verified skills | 25% | Assessments, certifications, work samples |
| Interview performance | 20% | Mock and real interviews, communication |
| Experience quality | 15% | Tenure, company tier, role progression |
| Education and credentials | 10% | Degrees, courses, verified credentials |
| Reliability signals | 10% | Response time, attendance, follow-through |
| Soft skills | 10% | Collaboration, leadership, adaptability |
| Market demand | 5% | Skills matched against current market needs |
| Growth trajectory | 5% | Learning velocity, skill acquisition rate |

## Required capabilities

- **Explainability.** "Why is my score 650?" answered per factor, in plain language.
- **Historical trend.** Is the candidate improving? Weekly and monthly snapshots.
- **Role-specific scores.** 700 for frontend, 550 for backend, not a single number.
- **Company-specific fit.** How well this candidate fits this specific company.
- **Peer comparison.** "Top 20% for your role", anonymised.
- **Improvement roadmap.** "Do X to gain roughly 50 points", with difficulty and time estimates.
- **Fraud detection.** Fake credentials and resume inflation.
- **Portability.** The candidate owns the score. It is not locked inside an employer's view.

## Fix the write loop first

`/candidate/omniscore` currently issues 70 POST writes to `omniscore/checkin` per page visit. That must be fixed before any of this ships. See the Phase 0 render loop issue.

## Data model

Store factor scores, historical snapshots, per-role and per-company variants. Analytics queries go to ClickHouse, operational reads stay in PostgreSQL. See the analytics store issue.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All 8 factors calculated with documented weights
- [ ] Every factor has a plain-language explanation visible to the candidate
- [ ] Historical trend chart with at least weekly granularity
- [ ] Role-specific and company-specific scores
- [ ] Peer percentile computed against the real pool
- [ ] Improvement roadmap with concrete actions and point estimates
- [ ] Fraud signals surfaced to recruiters and appealable by candidates
- [ ] Score calculation is deterministic and reproducible for audit
- [ ] Bias audit per factor, reported per job posting

issues.title: Chat and messaging between recruiters and candidates

## Problem

Both `/candidate/chat` and `/recruiter/chat` render a full chat UI, but every backing endpoint returns 404. Messaging is completely non-functional on both sides.

issues.title: Code sandbox - self-hosted Docker + Judge0 execution engine
issues.body:
## Requirement

Step 6 of the pipeline. A browser-based coding environment where candidates solve real problems, with server-side execution against test cases. Built in-house, no HackerRank or CodeSignal.

Architecture decided in the CEO review: **Docker + Judge0**, full language support from day one.

## Components

| Layer | Technology |
|---|---|
| Editor | Monaco, the VS Code editor, free and familiar |
| Execution | Judge0 on self-hosted Docker |
| Languages | JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Java, C++, Go, SQL |
| Grading | Hidden test cases plus AI code review |

## Security requirements, non-negotiable

Running untrusted code is the most dangerous thing in this codebase. Every one of these is mandatory:

- Network isolation, no outbound requests from the execution container
- Filesystem isolation, container-only, no host mounts
- Memory limit per execution
- CPU limit per execution
- Wall-clock timeout with hard kill
- No privileged operations, no root
- A fresh container per execution, zero state leakage between candidates
- Rate limiting per user to prevent the sandbox being used as free compute

A dedicated security audit must pass before this is exposed publicly. Tracked as a separate issue.

## Candidate experience

- Syntax highlighting, autocomplete, and a familiar keybinding set
- Run against sample test cases as often as they like
- Submit once, graded against hidden test cases
- Draft autosaved continuously, survives a disconnect
- Countdown timer with auto-submit

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All seven languages execute correctly
- [ ] Every security control above verified by a test that attempts to break it
- [ ] A fork bomb, an infinite loop, and an outbound network call are all contained
- [ ] Execution completes within the time limit or is killed cleanly
- [ ] Candidate draft survives refresh and disconnect
- [ ] Load test: 50 concurrent executions without degradation

Blocks the technical test templates and auto-grading issues.

Effort: ~60h

issues.title: Security audit of the code sandbox before public exposure
issues.body:
## Why

Agreed in the CEO review: the code sandbox does not go live until a dedicated security audit passes. Arbitrary code execution is the highest-risk surface we will ever ship.

## Scope

Attempt to break every control, and document the result of each attempt:

- Container escape
- Host filesystem access
- Outbound network access from inside the sandbox
- Resource exhaustion: fork bomb, memory bomb, infinite loop, disk fill
- State leakage between two candidates' executions
- Using the sandbox as free compute, for example crypto mining
- Reading another candidate's submission or test cases
- Privilege escalation inside the container
- Judge0 API abuse from an authenticated candidate account

## Deliverable

A written report listing each attack attempted, the outcome, and any remediation applied. Filed in `docs/security/`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every attack above attempted and documented
- [ ] No critical or high finding left open
- [ ] Report committed to `docs/security/`
- [ ] Sign-off recorded before the sandbox is enabled in production

Depends on the code sandbox issue.

Effort: ~16h

issues.title: Technical test templates and auto-grading
issues.body:
## Requirement

A library of role-specific coding challenges plus the grading engine that scores them. Crossover calls the equivalent "Real Work Assessments", and grades them against a detailed rubric.

## Scope

**Templates**
- Predefined challenges per role: frontend, backend, data, SQL, algorithms
- Difficulty tiers
- Recruiters can author custom challenges

**Auto-grading**

- Combined score with a written breakdown
- Plagiarism check against previous submissions

**Explainability**
- The candidate sees why they scored what they scored
- Which test cases passed and which failed, without leaking the hidden cases themselves

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Template library covers at least five role types
- [ ] Recruiters can author and preview a custom challenge
- [ ] Partial credit computed correctly across test cases
- [ ] AI code review produces a written, specific critique
- [ ] Plagiarism detection flags near-identical submissions

Depends on the code sandbox.

issues.title: Proctored assessment system - identity verification and anti-cheat
issues.body:
## Requirement

Approved as a scope expansion in the CEO review. This is Crossover's PCCAT equivalent, the final integrity check before an offer.

## Scope

**Identity verification**
- Photo ID capture and face match against the live webcam feed
- 360-degree room scan before the test starts

**Live monitoring**
- Webcam and screen recording for the duration
- Optional second camera via phone for a wider view
- Recording retained under the data retention policy, then purged

**Automated cheat detection**
- Tab and window switching
- Copy and paste events
- Multiple faces or no face in frame
- Audio anomalies suggesting a second person
- Timing anomalies against the candidate's own earlier unproctored result

**Review**
- Flagged sessions queued for human review, never auto-rejected by the AI alone
- The candidate is told they were flagged and why, and can respond

## Privacy and consent

Biometric data and recordings are the most sensitive data on the platform.

- Explicit, specific consent before recording starts, with a clear explanation of what is captured and how long it is kept
- Encrypted at rest
- Retention limit enforced automatically
- Right to deletion honoured
- GDPR and India DPDP compliance
- An accessible alternative path for candidates who cannot use proctoring, so we do not exclude people with disabilities or without suitable hardware

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Face match against ID works and is measured for accuracy across skin tones
- [ ] All cheat signals above detected and logged
- [ ] Flagged sessions go to human review, never auto-reject
- [ ] Consent captured before any recording begins
- [ ] Recordings encrypted and auto-purged on schedule
- [ ] Accessible alternative path documented and available

issues.title: AI Career Coach for candidates
issues.body:
## Requirement

## Features

| Feature | What it does |
|---|---|
| Career path recommendations | Where this candidate could go next, based on their profile and market data |

Every recommendation must be grounded in real data from the platform: actual job postings, actual skill demand, the candidate's own OmniScore factors. Generic LLM career advice is worthless and will not retain a subscriber.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Skill gap analysis cites specific open jobs the candidate would qualify for
- [ ] Career path suggestions reference real progression data

issues.title: TrustScore v2 - deep company scoring and accountability
issues.body:
## Why this matters

This is the half of the two-sided promise that no competitor delivers. Candidates are scored constantly. Companies are not. Glassdoor is gameable and stale. TrustScore is computed from behaviour we can observe directly on the platform.

Approved as a scope expansion in the CEO review.

## Factors

| Factor | Measured from |
|---|---|
| Employee satisfaction | Ratings and post-hire feedback |
| Interview experience | Candidate reviews of the process |
| Offer acceptance rate | Do candidates actually say yes |
| Time to hire | Speed from application to decision |
| Response rate | Do they reply, or do they ghost |
| Salary competitiveness | Offers against market rate for the role and location |
| Diversity metrics | Representation across the pipeline |
| Career growth | Progression of people they hired |

Response rate deserves emphasis. Ghosting is the top candidate complaint in every 2026 survey, and it is directly measurable on our platform. Making it public creates real pressure to fix it.

## Features

- Public company leaderboard
- Company-to-company comparison
- AI-generated "what it is like to work here" summary, grounded in the factor data
- Candidate reviews of the interview process, collected after a decision
- Companies can see their own breakdown and what to improve

## Fairness

- A company with too little data shows "not enough data", never a misleadingly precise number
- Review brigading detection
- Companies can respond publicly to a review
- The scoring methodology is published

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All eight factors computed from real platform data
- [ ] Ghosting and response rate visible to candidates before they apply
- [ ] Leaderboard and comparison views work
- [ ] Low-data companies show an honest "insufficient data" state
- [ ] Companies see their own breakdown and improvement guidance
- [ ] Methodology documented publicly

Builds on `routes/trustscore.js` and migration 002.

issues.title: Multi-interviewer panel with scorecards and shared notes
issues.body:
## Requirement

Steps 7 and 8 of the pipeline. Multiple interviewers, including the hiring manager, in one session with structured evaluation.

## Scope

- Multiple interviewers in a single interview room
- Participant tiles with role labels
- Shared notes visible to the panel during the interview
- Private notes visible only to their author
- Structured scorecard per interviewer, defined by the job
- Scores hidden from other interviewers until everyone submits, to prevent anchoring
- Aggregate panel recommendation after all scorecards are in
- Candidate never sees interviewer notes or scores

## Why hide scores until submission

Anchoring is a well-documented failure mode in panel interviews. If the first interviewer posts a 4, the rest converge on it. Independent submission then reveal is the standard fix.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Multiple interviewers join and are labelled correctly
- [ ] Shared and private notes both work and are correctly scoped
- [ ] Scorecards are hidden until all are submitted
- [ ] Aggregate recommendation computed after reveal
- [ ] Candidate has no access to notes or scores, verified by test

issues.title: Calendar integration and automated interview scheduling
issues.body:
## Requirement

Note: Google and Outlook OAuth are calendar protocol integrations, not a third-party hiring service, so they are in scope under the all-in-one principle.

issues.title: In-house e-signature engine with PKCS#7 cryptographic sealing
issues.body:
## Requirement

Step 10 of the pipeline. Legally binding electronic signatures, built in-house. Confirmed in the CEO review.

Legal validity comes from the process and the evidence trail, not from the vendor brand. We need to get the process right.

## Document preparation

- Templates for offer letter, contract, NDA, I-9, W-4
- Auto-fill from the candidate profile
- Drag and drop placement of signature and initial fields
- Multi-party signing with a defined order

## Signing ceremony

- Draw a signature with touch or mouse
- Type a signature with font choices
- Upload a signature image
- Initials per page where required
- Explicit intent-to-sign confirmation

## Cryptographic sealing

- PKCS#7 detached signature over the document hash
- Timestamp authority for a provable signing time
- Document hash stored so tampering is detectable afterwards
- Certificate of completion generated on finalisation

## Evidence trail

Every event recorded: sent, viewed, signed, declined, with timestamp, IP address, user agent and authenticated identity. This is what makes the signature defensible.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All three signature capture methods work
- [ ] Multi-party sequential signing works
- [ ] PKCS#7 signature verifies against the document
- [ ] Timestamp authority applied
- [ ] Any post-signature modification is detectable
- [ ] Certificate of completion generated and downloadable
- [ ] Full evidence trail recorded and exportable
- [ ] Signed documents encrypted at rest

Builds on migration 024 offer letter generation.

Effort: ~40h

issues.title: Background check - identity verification
issues.body:
## Requirement

Step 11 of the pipeline, identity component. Self-hosted, no Checkr or Sterling.

## Scope

- Government ID upload: passport, driver licence, national ID
- OCR extraction of name, date of birth, document number, expiry
- Face match between the ID photo and a live selfie
- Liveness detection to defeat a photo held up to the camera
- Expiry and validity checks
- Cross-check extracted details against the candidate's profile

## Accuracy and fairness

Face matching has a well-documented accuracy gap across skin tones and genders. We must measure our own false-reject rate across demographic groups and publish it internally. A failed automated match must route to human review, never to automatic rejection.

## Data handling

Government ID images are the most sensitive data we will hold.

- Encrypted at rest with AES-256
- Access logged, every view attributed
- Retention limit, auto-purge after the configured window
- Right to deletion honoured
- Recruiters see verification status, not the raw ID image

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] OCR extracts fields correctly across at least three ID types
- [ ] Face match works, with false-reject rate measured across demographic groups
- [ ] Liveness detection defeats a printed photo and a screen replay
- [ ] Failed matches go to human review, never auto-reject
- [ ] Images encrypted, access logged, retention enforced
- [ ] Recruiter view shows status only, never the raw image

Effort: ~40h

issues.title: Background check - employment and education verification
issues.body:
## Requirement

Step 11 of the pipeline, history component.

## Employment verification

- Candidate declares employment history with contactable references
- Automated verification request sent to the former employer
- Structured response form for the employer: dates, title, eligibility for rehire
- Manual fallback when the employer does not respond
- Discrepancy detection against the resume and profile

## Education verification

- Degree and certificate upload
- OCR extraction of institution, qualification, dates
- Verification request to the institution where a contact exists
- Manual review fallback

## Reference checks

- Structured reference questionnaire
- Reference responses collected and summarised

## Fairness

A discrepancy is not automatically fraud. Job titles change, companies get acquired, records are imperfect. Every discrepancy must be shown to the candidate with an opportunity to explain before it reaches the recruiter as a negative signal.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Verification requests sent and responses recorded
- [ ] Manual fallback path works when there is no response
- [ ] Discrepancies detected and surfaced to the candidate first
- [ ] Candidate can respond to a discrepancy before the recruiter sees a conclusion
- [ ] Reference questionnaire collected and summarised
- [ ] Full audit trail

Effort: ~40h

issues.title: Document OCR and fraud detection
issues.body:
## Scope

- OCR across document types: IDs, degrees, certificates, payslips
- Structured field extraction
- Tamper detection: inconsistent fonts, misaligned text, digital editing artefacts, metadata anomalies
- Template matching against known genuine document layouts
- Cross-document consistency, for example the same name and date of birth everywhere
- Confidence score per document

## Fairness

A fraud flag is an accusation. It must be reviewable, explainable and appealable:

- Every flag states exactly what triggered it
- Flags go to human review, never to automatic rejection
- The candidate is told a document was flagged and can respond or resubmit
- False positive rate tracked

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] OCR accurate across at least five document types
- [ ] Tamper detection catches a deliberately edited test document
- [ ] Cross-document inconsistency detected
- [ ] Every flag carries a specific stated reason
- [ ] Human review required before any adverse action
- [ ] Candidate can appeal and resubmit
- [ ] False positive rate measured

Builds on `services/document-verification.js`.

Effort: ~36h

issues.title: Aadhaar verification for the India market
issues.body:
## Requirement

India-specific identity verification. India is our first market, so this matters more than the generic ID flow.

## Scope

- Aadhaar number entry with checksum validation
- OTP verification flow to the registered mobile number
- Masked Aadhaar display, never show or store the full number in plain form
- Offline Aadhaar XML verification as an alternative path
- PAN card verification

## Legal and privacy constraints

Aadhaar handling is tightly regulated in India. Get this wrong and it is a legal problem, not just a security one.

- Never store the full Aadhaar number, store only a masked form and a hash
- Explicit purpose-limited consent before collection
- Comply with the Aadhaar Act and the DPDP Act
- Access logged and auditable
- Retention limits enforced
- The candidate must have a non-Aadhaar alternative, since Aadhaar cannot be made mandatory for private employment

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Checksum validation rejects malformed numbers
- [ ] OTP flow completes end to end
- [ ] Full Aadhaar number never stored or displayed
- [ ] Offline XML path works as an alternative
- [ ] Explicit consent captured before collection
- [ ] Non-Aadhaar alternative available and documented
- [ ] Legal review completed before this ships

Effort: ~24h

issues.title: Compliance audit trail across verification and AI decisions
issues.body:
## Requirement

A single, tamper-evident audit trail covering every consequential action, needed for EU AI Act compliance and for defending any hiring decision that is later challenged.

## What must be logged

- Every AI decision: inputs, outputs, model version, timestamp
- Every human override of an AI decision, with the reason
- Every access to sensitive candidate data, attributed to a user
- Every verification step and its outcome
- Every signature event
- Every status change in the hiring pipeline

## Properties

- Append-only, no updates or deletes
- Tamper-evident via hash chaining
- Exportable for regulators
- Queryable by candidate, by job, by recruiter, by date range
- Retained beyond the operational data retention window, since audit records outlive the data they describe

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All six event categories logged
- [ ] Log is append-only, verified by test
- [ ] Hash chain detects tampering
- [ ] Export produces a regulator-ready report
- [ ] Queryable across all four dimensions
- [ ] A candidate can request the full record of decisions about them

Builds on `routes/compliance.js` and migration 013.

Effort: ~20h

- [ ] CSV and Excel both import correctly
- [ ] Column mapping handles arbitrary source formats
- [ ] Validation errors reported per row before commit
- [ ] Duplicates detected and mergeable
- [ ] Dry run shows exactly what will happen
- [ ] Completed import can be rolled back
- [ ] A 10,000 row import completes without timeout

Effort: ~16h

issues.title: EU AI Act compliance dashboard and regulatory reporting
issues.body:
## Requirement

Hiring AI is classified as high-risk under the EU AI Act. Completing this properly is both a legal requirement for the EU market and a genuine competitive advantage, since most competitors are still scrambling.

Current state is roughly 50%. The framework exists in `routes/compliance.js`, `services/biasDetection.js` and `admin/compliance.tsx`, but needs completion and legal validation.

## Scope

- Risk classification self-assessment
- Bias detection reporting **per job posting**, not aggregated. The Stanford research showed aggregated audits are exactly how vendors hide adverse impact.
- Four-fifths rule calculation per posting
- Explainability panel: why the AI scored a given candidate the way it did
- Human oversight controls with override capability and audit trail
- Data retention policy display
- Candidate consent management for AI processing
- Exportable transparency reports for regulators
- Legal review before the EU market opens

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Bias reporting is per posting, with four-fifths rule applied
- [ ] Explainability panel covers every AI decision type on the platform
- [ ] Human override available and audit logged everywhere AI makes a recommendation
- [ ] Candidate consent captured and revocable
- [ ] Transparency report exportable in a regulator-ready format
- [ ] Legal review completed and signed off

Effort: ~24h

issues.title: ClickHouse analytics store alongside operational PostgreSQL
issues.body:
## Requirement

Decided in the CEO review: PostgreSQL remains the operational database, ClickHouse handles analytics.

## Why

OmniScore v2 stores factor scores, historical snapshots, per-role and per-company variants for every candidate. Peer percentile calculations are aggregate queries across the whole pool. Running those against the operational database will degrade the transactional path as the pool grows.

## Scope

- Deploy ClickHouse
- Replication pipeline from PostgreSQL, CDC or scheduled batch
- Move OmniScore historical and percentile queries to ClickHouse
- Move the analytics dashboard queries to ClickHouse
- Retention and partitioning strategy
- Backup and restore

## Rollback plan

ClickHouse adds real operational overhead. Keep the PostgreSQL query paths intact behind a feature flag so we can fall back if the ops burden outweighs the benefit at current scale.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] ClickHouse deployed with backups configured
- [ ] Replication lag under one minute
- [ ] Percentile queries return in under 500ms at 100k candidate scale
- [ ] Analytics dashboard reads from ClickHouse
- [ ] Feature flag allows fallback to PostgreSQL
- [ ] Restore from backup tested

Blocks OmniScore v2 percentiles and the advanced analytics dashboard.

Effort: ~24h

issues.title: Self-hosted observability - Prometheus, Grafana and Loki
issues.body:
## Requirement

Decided in the CEO review: fully self-hosted monitoring, consistent with the all-in-one principle.

We currently have no production error monitoring at all. We are blind.

## Scope

- Prometheus for metrics
- Grafana for dashboards
- Loki for log aggregation
- Alertmanager for alerting

## Metrics needed

- Error rate by endpoint and by user
- API latency p50, p95, p99
- Request volume per page, which is how we catch the next render loop automatically
- Code sandbox execution time and failure rate
- Video call quality
- OmniScore calculation latency
- Database query performance
- AI provider latency, cost and failure rate

## Alerts

- 5xx rate above 1%
- p95 latency above 1 second
- Any endpoint receiving an anomalous request volume, which would have caught the 1,255-call loop on day one
- AI provider failures exhausting the fallback chain
- Disk, memory and connection pool saturation

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All four components deployed
- [ ] Every metric above collected
- [ ] Every alert above configured and tested by deliberately triggering it
- [ ] Dashboards for API health, AI health and business funnel
- [ ] Alerts route to a channel that a human actually reads

Effort: ~24h

issues.title: Raise E2E test coverage to 95%
issues.body:
## Target

95% E2E coverage, agreed in the CEO review. Current coverage is roughly 55%.

## Gaps to close

- Code sandbox execution across all languages
- Multi-party video interview flow
- E-signature ceremony end to end
- BGC verification workflow
- Proctored assessment flow
- OmniScore calculation accuracy against known fixtures
- TrustScore aggregation
- Screening and aptitude flows
- Recruiter approval workflow, including privilege escalation attempts
- Per-page API request count budget, which is the regression guard for the render loop bug

## Infrastructure work

The full Playwright suite currently cannot run in one pass due to browser resource limits, and is worked around by running per file. Fix this so CI runs the whole suite.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] 95% coverage measured and reported in CI
- [ ] Full suite runs in a single CI job without resource failures
- [ ] Request count budget test in place for every page
- [ ] Suite runs on every pull request
- [ ] Flaky tests quarantined rather than retried blindly

Effort: ~40h

issues.title: Code split the 1.55MB main bundle
issues.body:
## Problem

The main client chunk is 1.55MB across 1719 modules. On a mid-range Android phone on Indian mobile data, that is a multi-second parse before anything renders. India is our first market and it is mobile-first.

This is also a likely contributor to the 6.1 second post-auth redirect.

## Scope

- Route-level code splitting
- Dynamic import for heavy pages: interviews, analytics, admin, onboarding
- Tree-shake unused dependencies, check whether `nodemailer` is genuinely needed in client deps
- Verify gzip or Brotli compression is active

## Target

- No chunk above 500KB
- First contentful paint under 1.5 seconds on a throttled 4G connection
- Time to interactive under 3 seconds

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Largest chunk under 500KB
- [ ] FCP under 1.5s on throttled 4G
- [ ] TTI under 3s
- [ ] Bundle size budget enforced in CI

Effort: ~12h

issues.title: Sanitise AI-generated HTML before storage and rendering
issues.body:
## Problem

AI-generated HTML is stored unsanitised and later rendered with `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`. That is a stored XSS path.

| Location | Issue |
|---|---|
| `routes/onboarding.js:105` | AI HTML stored unsanitised |
| `routes/recruiter.js:2122` | AI HTML stored unsanitised |
| `client/src/pages/blog.tsx:356` | `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` |
| `client/src/pages/recruiter/onboarding-docs.tsx:383` | `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` |

Also outstanding: OAuth tokens are stored in plaintext at `routes/auth.js:479` and `routes/auth.js:629`, despite `lib/crypto-utils.js` existing for exactly this purpose.

## Scope

- Sanitise with DOMPurify before database storage, defence in depth
- Sanitise again before render
- Apply `lib/crypto-utils.js` encryption to OAuth token storage
- Add a Content Security Policy

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All four HTML locations sanitised on both write and render
- [ ] A stored XSS payload in an AI-generated document does not execute
- [ ] OAuth tokens encrypted at rest
- [ ] CSP header present and tested
- [ ] Lint rule flags any new `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`

Effort: ~8h
